page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM, running on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only small block bandwidth rated as poor and large block read/write bandwidth categorized as weak. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core, the c2d-highcpu-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is suitable for single-threaded processing, basic text processing, lightweight web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks utilizing small models, where prompt processing and text generation speeds remain within average to weak thresholds. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or highly parallelized multi-core workloads.
